subject: Forest plot y-axis in log scale

messages.author: 16524dc094cde87d
messages.subject: Forest plot y-axis in log scale
parts:
Hi,

  I am plotting a forest plot using the following command. But the y axis comes out as linear. I tried using scale_y_log10 but that didn't solve the problem. Any help is appreciated.

Thanks,

Here's how the data looks like:

############# Data #############
x y ylo yhi
AA 0.98 0.85 1.13
AD I 1.13 0.97 1.30
DD II 1.20 0.93 1.54
AC III 1.03 0.89 1.20
DN 1.02 0.77 1.35
ADA 1.17 0.99 1.40
AY 1.21 1.05 1.39

where x=study, y=Odds Ratio, ylo and yhi are the lower and upper confidence limits for y

############# Code ############
d<-read.table("hit1.txt", header=T, sep="\t")
d$x <- factor(d$x, levels = rev((as.character(d$x))))
ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, ymin=ylo, ymax=yhi)) +
geom_pointrange(size=0.75, shape=18) +
coord_flip() +
geom_hline(yintercept=1, linetype="dashed", lwd=0.7) +
scale_y_continuous(name="Odds Ratio", breaks=c(0.80, 1.0, 1.20, 1.40, 1.60, 1.80)) +
xlab("Study") +
theme(axis.title.x = element_text(size=14), axis.title.y = element_text(size=14), axis.text.x=element_text(face="bold", colour="black"), axis.text.y=element_text(face="bold",colour="black"))

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Forest plot y-axis in log scale
parts:
ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, ymin=ylo, ymax=yhi)) +
geom_pointrange(size=0.75, shape=18) +

coord_flip() +
xlab("Study") +
theme(axis.title = element_text(size=14),
axis.text = element_text(face="bold", colour="black"))

If you look carefully, you'll see that the log-transformation is
applied because the widths between axis ticks on the (log) odds ratio
scale are not equal. ggplot2 uses the values in the original scale as
the axis ticks but the scale in which they are rendered is log_10,
which you can tell by the spacing between the grid lines. See the
examples at the bottom of
http://docs.ggplot2.org/current/scale_continuous.html for further
illustration of this idea.

If you want the plot to be linear in the log10 scale, you could do
something like this:

ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=log10(y), ymin=log10(ylo), ymax=log10(yhi))) +
geom_pointrange(size=0.75, shape=18) +
geom_hline(yintercept=0, linetype="dashed", lwd=0.7) +
scale_y_continuous(name="Log Odds Ratio", limits = c(-0.15, 0.25),
breaks= seq(-0.1, 0.2, by = 0.1)) +
coord_flip() +
xlab("Study") +
theme(axis.title = element_text(size=14),
axis.text = element_text(face="bold", colour="black"))

(Aside: Notice the abridgement of the theme() call - the new theming
system applies inheritance of theme properties, so it's sufficient in
this case to apply element_text() to axis.title and axis.text rather
than to both the x and y versions thereof.)

This would be the 'simple' way to do it. The alternative is to start
playing around in the scales package. A short introduction is given
here: http://cloud.github.com/downloads/hadley/ggplot2/guide-col.pdf
(see section 7) but some advances have been made since it was written
nearly a year ago. Also see Brian Diggs' posts on defining scales at
the ggplot2 blog:http://blog.ggplot2.org/ The latter of the two posts
is near the top, which contains a link to the first post.

Dennis
